html:
In 1654 the Duchy of Courland, a small Baltic state in what is now Latvia, founded a colony on Tobago, naming its harbour Great Courland Bay. It was one of the strangest outposts of the colonial age.

Duke Jacob Kettler also held a fort in the Gambia in West Africa. The Courlanders traded and planted, but the Dutch took the colony in 1659.

Tobago then passed between the Dutch, French, English and Courlanders more often than almost any Caribbean island. Britain held it for good from 1814 and in 1889 joined it to Trinidad, as told under Tobago. A monument at Plymouth recalls the Latvian settlers.
